- Channel 1 (moving objects) has very large weights at border cells: (5,0) 16.86 and (7,9) 15.51, with other strong border-adjacent weights at (8,5) 14.76, (0,1) 9.47, (1,5) 7.19. These look like tunnel entrances where moving objects can leave/enter the playable area.  
- Channel 2 (reward targets) has high weights at scattered cells: (1,2) 14.82, (2,4) 14.43, (7,3) 16.41, (8,9) 15.28, (5,9) 10.87, (3,7) 8.41. This matches pellets/power pellets distributed through a maze.  
- Channel 3 (obstacles) has large weights on the wall border and inner wall-like cells: (5,0) 11.16, (5,1) 14.30, (0,3) 10.61, (0,4) 7.82, (8,0) 6.38, (8,1) 5.35, (9,3) 4.91, (9,4) 5.15, (9,9) 5.14. This is consistent with a fixed maze layout.  
- Output bias b3 strongly favours action 1 (up): b3[1] = 3.142, while down is -1.862, right -1.269. This fits an agent that often starts near the bottom and needs to move upward into the maze.  
- Top W1 connections repeatedly involve (r5,c0,ch1) and (r7,c9,ch1), i.e. moving objects at the left/right border tunnels.

Reasoning:  
The five channels exactly match a grid-based Pac-Man: agent = Pac-Man, moving objects = ghosts, reward targets = pellets, obstacles = maze walls, previous frame = movement history. The actions are exactly no-op, up, down, left, right, which are Pac-Manâs controls. The large weights for moving objects on the border are only sensible if there are tunnels on the left/right edges, a defining feature of Pac-Man. Other games are ruled out: Sokoban has no autonomous moving objects; Snake has no separate moving objects; Bomberman would need a bomb action; Frogger has no tunnels and a different reward structure.

Game: Pac-Man (a simplified grid-based Pac-Man).

Description: The agent controls Pac-Man in a maze, moving up/down/left/right to eat pellets (reward targets) while avoiding ghosts (moving objects). Eating pellets gives reward, and colliding with a ghost ends the episode.

Confidence: 92%
